name: THS4521IDGKR
title: Very low power fully differential amplifier, negative-rail input, rail-to-rail output (single, dual, quad)
summary: THS4521 (one channel), THS4522 (two) and THS4524 (four) are voltage-feedback fully differential amplifiers drawing about 1 mA per channel from a single 2.5 V to 5.5 V supply. The input common-mode range reaches below the negative rail and the outputs swing rail to rail, so a ground-referenced single-ended source can be turned into a differential signal centred on a VOCM level for a SAR or delta-sigma ADC. Each channel has a VOCM pin that sets the output common mode (midsupply when open) and a PD pin that cuts the channel current to 10 µA (3.3 V) or 20 µA (5 V).
key_figures: 1.14 mA per channel typ at 5 V
490 V/µs rising, 600 V/µs falling at 5 V

circuits.title: THS4521 driving the ADS1278 24-bit delta-sigma ADC
circuits.description: A single 5-V THS4521 at unity gain (1 kΩ in, 1 kΩ back) turns a differential input into the drive for one ADS1278 channel. Each output reaches the ADC through 49.9 Ω, with 2.2 nF across the ADC inputs; the feedback resistors are taken from the ADC side of those resistors, while 1.5 nF runs from each summing node to the amplifier output pin. The ADC common-mode output VCOM, bypassed with 0.1 µF, is buffered by half an OPA2350 and drives VOCM, which has its own 0.1 µF to ground, so the output common mode follows the ADC VCOM.
notes: PD is not connected (open runs the amplifier). The OPA2350 supply and its feedback connection are not drawn.

circuits.title: THS4521 driving the ADS8321 16-bit SAR ADC
circuits.description: A 5-V THS4521 at unity gain with 1-kΩ input and feedback resistors drives the ADS8321 inputs through 49.9 Ω per side. At the converter each input has 68 pF to ground and 1 nF sits across the pair. VOCM is left open with 0.22 µF to ground, so the outputs default to midsupply.
notes: PD is not connected.

circuits.title: THS4521 driving a PCM4204 audio ADC input (EVM channel)
circuits.description: One channel of the PCM4204 evaluation board with its original driver replaced by a THS4521 on a single 5-V supply. Inputs enter through 1 kΩ; 270-Ω feedback resistors close the loop from beyond the 40.2-Ω output resistors, and 1 nF runs from each summing node to the near output pin; the gain is 0.27. The outputs reach the ADC through 0-Ω links, with 2.7 nF across the ADC inputs and 100 pF from each to ground. VOCM has 0.1 µF to ground and floats, so the outputs sit at 2.5 V. The positive supply has 10 µF and 0.01 µF to ground.
notes: On the board the positive supply pin was moved from +15 V to +5 V and the negative supply pin from –15 V to ground, so C30 and C42 have both ends on ground.
R27 (1 kΩ), which joins VOCM to the PCM4204 common-mode output, is removed; fitting it made no difference.
For gains of 1, 2 and 5 the feedback resistors R33 and R34 are changed.
PD is not connected.

circuits.title: THS4521EVM evaluation board
circuits.description: The evaluation board: a THS4521 set for unity gain with 1-kΩ gain and feedback resistors, a 50-Ω terminated single-ended input on J2 and a transformer-coupled single-ended output on J9. The input side carries 52.3 Ω to ground at each gain resistor, a 0-Ω path past the unfitted input transformer T1, and on J1 a 0.22 µF plus 49.9 Ω to ground that balances the unused input. Each output drives 487 Ω into the primary of the ADT1-1WT, with 52.3 Ω across it; one secondary end goes to J9 through 0 Ω and the other to ground through 0 Ω. PD and VOCM each have 0.22 µF to ground and their own connectors; the JP1 shunt ties PD to VS– to switch the amplifier off. Each supply has 10 µF and 0.1 µF capacitors to ground. Parts marked open are footprints left empty.
notes: Connector pin 1 is the centre or signal contact, pin 2 the shell. Transformer pins carry their package numbers: T1 primary 3-2-1, secondary 4-5-6; T2 primary 6-5-4, secondary 1-2-3.
C3, C5, C11 and C12 are 0603 and C7 to C10 are 0805 parts.

circuits.title: AC-coupled single-ended 50-Ω source to differential, gain of 2 V/V
circuits.description: A 50-Ω source is terminated by Rt = 52.3 Ω and AC-coupled through 100 nF into Rg1 = 499 Ω; the other gain resistor, Rg2 = 523 Ω, returns to ground through a matching 100 nF so both feedback dividers stay balanced and no DC flows from the output common mode. With 1.02-kΩ feedback the gain from the Rt node to the differential output is 2 V/V into a 500-Ω load, while the input stays matched to 50 Ω.
notes: VOCM is drawn unconnected, so the outputs default to midsupply. PD is tied to Vcc.

circuits.title: DC-coupled single-ended 50-Ω source to differential, gain of 5 V/V
circuits.description: The DC-coupled form: Rt = 59 Ω terminates the 50-Ω source, Rg1 = 187 Ω feeds the inverting input, Rg2 = 215 Ω goes straight to ground, and 1-kΩ feedback resistors set a gain of 5 V/V from the Rt node to a 500-Ω differential load. Because both sides are DC-coupled, a common-mode current flows from the outputs back through the feedback and gain resistors to the source and ground, which lifts the input pins above ground.
notes: VOCM is drawn unconnected, so the outputs default to midsupply. PD is tied to Vcc.

circuits.title: Single-ended to differential, 200-Ω input impedance, gain of 4 V/V
circuits.description: Driven from a low-impedance source with no termination resistor, equal 120-Ω gain resistors (one to the source, one to ground) and 480-Ω feedback give a gain of 4 V/V into 500 Ω. Because the input pins follow the signal in common mode, the source sees about 200 Ω rather than 120 Ω. For AC coupling, a blocking capacitor goes in series with each 120-Ω resistor.
notes: VOCM is drawn unconnected; PD is tied to Vcc.

circuits.title: AC-coupled differential input from a down-converting mixer
circuits.description: A mixer differential output is coupled through two 100-nF capacitors. Rm = 125 Ω across the pair after the capacitors, in parallel with the 500 Ω the two 250-Ω gain resistors present, gives the source a 100-Ω AC termination. 1-kΩ feedback closes each side, and the outputs drive 500 Ω. With no DC path from the outputs, the VOCM voltage also sets the input common mode.
notes: VOCM is drawn unconnected; PD is tied to Vcc.

circuits.title: DC-coupled single-supply operation with a single-ended source
circuits.description: A ground-referenced source drives RG into the noninverting input, terminated by RIT; the inverting side has a matching RG and RIT to ground, plus an optional series RC to ground that balances the impedance seen at the signal input. RF closes each side and RO isolates each output. VS– is grounded, so the amplifier runs from one supply; the input common-mode range includes ground. VOCM and PD each have 0.22 µF to ground and are driven by external control voltages; VOCM left open defaults to midsupply. The same circuit accepts a differential source.

circuits.title: Differential input to differential output amplifier
circuits.description: The basic differential stage: equal RG resistors from the two inputs and equal RF resistors from each output back to the opposite-polarity input. The differential gain is RF / RG and the differential input impedance is the sum of the two RG resistors.
notes: VOCM and PD are not drawn.

circuits.title: Single-ended input to differential output amplifier
circuits.description: The single-ended form: the signal drives one RG into the noninverting input and the matching RG on the other side goes to ground. RF from each output to the opposite input sets a gain of RF / RG.
notes: VOCM and PD are not drawn.

circuits.title: Frequency response test circuit
circuits.description: A DC-coupled 50-Ω network analyzer drives RG, with RIT chosen for the gain and a 50-Ω match; the unused input has its own RG and RIT plus 49.9 Ω to ground. 1-kΩ feedback on both sides. The outputs drive 24.9 Ω each into 953 Ω, and a high-impedance differential probe across the 953 Ω reads the response, 0.42 dB below the amplifier output.
notes: PD and VOCM are left open, each with 0.22 µF to ground. Supply bypassing is not drawn.
RG and RIT for each gain are in the gain component values table.

circuits.title: Harmonic and intermodulation distortion test circuit
circuits.description: An AC-coupled 50-Ω signal generator, with a low-pass filter ahead of it, drives RG; RIT matches 50 Ω and the other input is balanced with 0.22 µF in series with 49.9 Ω to ground. Each output goes through RO, ROT sits across the pair, and a 1:1 ADT1-1WT transformer turns the differential signal into a single-ended one for a spectrum analyzer; a notch filter removes the fundamental there. The transformer stops measurements below about 1 MHz.
notes: PD and VOCM are left open, each with 0.22 µF to ground. Supply bypassing is not drawn.
RG, RF and RIT follow the gain table; RO and ROT follow the load table for the 1:1 transformer.

circuits.title: Slew rate, transient, settling, output impedance, overdrive, swing and turn-on/off test circuit
circuits.description: The same 50-Ω input and balance network with 1-kΩ feedback; each output drives a 50-Ω oscilloscope input through 49.9 Ω. For turn-on and turn-off timing the 0.22 µF on PD is replaced by 49.9 Ω so PD presents 50 Ω to a pulse source. For output impedance the input is left open, a signal is injected at the output, and the drop across the two 49.9-Ω resistors gives the impedance.
notes: PD and VOCM are left open, each with 0.22 µF to ground. Supply bypassing is not drawn.

circuits.title: CMRR test circuit
circuits.description: The network analyzer drives both 1-kΩ input resistors together, terminated by 52.3 Ω, so the signal is pure common mode; 1-kΩ feedback on both sides with resistors matched. The output is read by a differential probe across 953 Ω fed through 24.9 Ω from each output, 0.42 dB below the amplifier output.
notes: PD and VOCM are left open, each with 0.22 µF to ground. Supply bypassing is not drawn.

circuits.title: PSRR test circuit
circuits.description: The supply under test feeds VS+ through the network analyzer DC-offset input, so the analyzer signal rides on the supply; a calibrated differential probe reads VS+ against ground. Both inputs are terminated with 52.3 Ω and fed through 1 kΩ, with 1-kΩ feedback. The output is read across 953 Ω fed through 24.9 Ω from each output. The same arrangement on VS– measures the negative-supply rejection.
notes: PD and VOCM are left open, each with 0.22 µF to ground. Supply bypassing is not drawn.

circuits.title: VOCM input test circuit
circuits.description: The signal inputs are terminated (49.9 Ω) and fed through 1 kΩ with 1-kΩ feedback. Two matched 499-Ω resistors from the outputs form their average at one node, where a differential probe measures the VOCM bandwidth. The network analyzer, terminated in 49.9 Ω, drives VOCM through RCM: 0 Ω for bandwidth, 10 kΩ for input impedance, which is worked out from the drop across that resistor.
notes: PD is left open with 0.22 µF to ground.

circuits.title: VOCM transient response and slew rate test circuit
circuits.description: A 1-V step, terminated in 49.9 Ω, drives VOCM directly. The two 499-Ω resistors average the outputs into a 50-Ω oscilloscope input with 49.9 Ω to ground at that node; the signal inputs are terminated in 52.3 Ω and fed through 1 kΩ with 1-kΩ feedback.
notes: PD is left open with 0.22 µF to ground.

circuits.title: Audio analyzer test circuit
circuits.description: Differential drive from the audio analyzer through 1-kΩ input resistors, 1-kΩ feedback, and 24.9 Ω in series with each output back to the analyzer. Used for THD+N, FFT and channel-to-channel crosstalk. A 10-Ω resistor across the two input terminals raises the noise gain to 101 for the low-distortion estimate.
notes: PD and VOCM are left open, each with 0.22 µF to ground. Supply bypassing is not drawn.

operation.text: A high-open-loop-gain differential amplifier drives OUT+ and OUT–. Two 5-kΩ resistors across the outputs sense their average, and a separate Vcm error amplifier compares that average with the VOCM voltage and corrects the main amplifier. VOCM is biased to midsupply by two 275-kΩ resistors, one to each supply. PD drives a CMOS buffer.

The amplifier needs external gain and feedback resistors to set gain and input impedance. With PD more than VS– + 1.7 V it runs; with PD low the quiescent current stops, but the source still sees a signal path through the external resistors.

PD is guaranteed on above 2.1 V and off below 0.7 V, with the switch point near 1.6 V; left open the channel runs. Disabled current is 10 µA at 3.3 V and 20 µA at 5 V; turn-on takes about 70 ns to 108 ns and turn-off 60 ns to 88 ns. PD uses TTL levels; a bypass capacitor on it is not needed when driven but helps in noisy surroundings. On the THS4522 and THS4524 each channel has its own PD.

The voltage on VOCM sets the output common mode, held to within about 5 mV typical of it. Left open, VOCM settles at midsupply through the internal divider, which an external source can overdrive. The VOCM loop has about 23 MHz of bandwidth but is meant as a DC input; 0.22 µF from VOCM to ground near the pin keeps noise out. Its usable range is about 0.91 V above the negative supply to 1.1 V below the positive supply.

The input pins sit at the input common-mode voltage, a few millivolts apart in linear operation. The range runs from below the negative rail (–0.2 V typ) to about 1.3 V below the positive rail (2 V on 3.3 V, 3.7 V on 5 V). The inputs need at least 1.2 V of headroom to the positive supply.

With a single-ended drive the input pins move in common mode with the signal, so the impedance seen at the signal-side gain resistor is higher than that resistor. AC-coupled input: the input common mode equals the output common mode, since no DC flows through the gain resistors. DC-coupled input: both gain resistors must be DC-coupled to keep the dividers balanced; VOCM then drives a DC current back through RF and RG into the source, which must sink or source it and which lifts the input pins off ground. Grounding RG2 suits a source swinging about ground; biasing it at the source midpoint centres the output swing on VOCM.

Each output swings ±VP = VOPP / 4 about VOCM, 180° apart; VOCM ± VP must stay inside the rails. Linear operation needs about 200 mV of headroom to each rail, although the output is rail-to-rail. For linear output down to ground a small negative supply can be used, for example the LM7705, which produces –230 mV from the 3-V to 5-V supply.

Larger gain and feedback resistors save power and load the source less, but lower the bandwidth through the device and board parasitic capacitance: with RF = RG = RL = 10 kΩ the response peaks by about 4 dB near 30 MHz and falls earlier than with 1 kΩ. Lower RF improves noise and phase margin but loads the outputs more; higher RF adds output noise and can reduce phase margin through the pole with the input capacitance.

Small-signal response differs between packages because of their parasitics and board layout: the THS4522 and THS4524 peak by about 3 dB near 100 MHz, the THS4521 in SOIC slightly, and the THS4521 in MSOP not at all.

The outputs are designed for about 1 pF to ground each. Larger loads need a small series resistor RO at each output, close to the pins; without it the load capacitance erodes phase margin, giving peaking, overshoot, ringing or oscillation. RO restores the margin at some cost in bandwidth; the recommended RO for a flat response runs from about 120 Ω at 10 pF to 7 Ω at 1000 pF.

Intended for a nominal single supply of 3 V to 5 V; the specified 2.5 V to 5.5 V covers 10% low on 3 V and 8% high on 5 V. Split supplies work while the total stays under the 5.5-V absolute maximum. Input and output ranges track the supply nearly one for one; slew rate, output current, open-loop gain, bandwidth and distortion change somewhat.

Performance is the same on 3.3-V and 5-V supplies. Measured on an audio analyzer, distortion is close to the analyzer floor; at a noise gain of 101 (10 Ω across the inputs) HD2 at 1 kHz, 1 VRMS is estimated at –122 dBc and HD3 at –141 dBc. HD2 depends strongly on cancellation, and so on layout, bypassing and cabling. No audible pop is heard when the supply or PD is switched, with or without a tone, and PD switching is faster.

Keep signal paths and the feedback path short and direct. Remove ground and power planes from under the input and output pins. Put a series resistor in each output lead close to the pin. Place two 0.1-µF supply capacitors as close to the supply pins as possible, and two 10-µF capacitors within 1 inch (these can be shared among analog parts). Place 0.22 µF from VOCM to ground near the pin. If the EVM input termination resistors R10 and R11 are used, return them to ground at a single point on layer 2.

Characterization uses split supplies and the THS4521 evaluation board, mostly with a single-ended input and a transformer on the output; single-supply and fully differential use give the same or better results. Supply bypassing is omitted from the test circuits. With an AC-coupled generator the unused input carries 0.22 µF and 49.9 Ω across its RIT; with a DC-coupled one, 49.9 Ω alone.
THS4524-EP, an enhanced-product version, is listed as another qualified version of the THS4521 and THS4524.
